title: Living stations and the law
summary: Patch 0018 brings the stations to life. Docking has no cut any more: the pad's lift carries your ship down into a port hung under the platform - a hall where the lifts come down, a concourse, and rooms with windows out to space: the services hall, a bar, a lounge, the harbour office, the stores. Its people are the empire's own; they work, carry crates, sit at the bar and their desks, and you can talk to them for news and work, or sit down yourself. Each terminal opens its own service. Stations are armed and keep the law - fines for firing on traders, their guns turned on a murderer - and enemy fleets besiege them, their warships firing on them until you answer the station's call. Every empire now has its own people, ships, stations and towns, its worlds lean to its own colours, the jet pack can take you into space, and the insides of ports and ships follow their outsides.

steps.title: Every empire its own
steps.text: Each empire now has its own people, ship designs, stations, hangar crews and town architecture, taken from its reference sheets: Athens' marble ring with temples, Sparta's iron fortress, Mycenae's citadel of great stones, Ionia's armillary, the Cyclades' marble spiral, the Sea Peoples' broken iron ring. The independents' crews come from every empire.

steps.title: A jump, and the jet pack
steps.text: The jump no longer flips: a push off, the knees drawn up, a fall with the arms out. Keep Space held and the jet pack on your back fires; upgraded through five levels it climbs higher and longer, and at the last it never runs out - out of the air into space, hovering when you let go, landing on another world with no ship.

steps.title: Dust, roar, heat haze - and the ship comes
steps.text: Landing kicks up dust in the ground's colour, and the jet raises it under you; a thud on landing and the jet's roar while it fires; heat haze bends the view below the nozzles. Fall more than a few storeys and it hurts - hold the jet to brake. Off the ground a marker shows your ship; flying free high up or in space, B brings it to you and you're aboard.

diagram.label:
falls over ~8 m
hurt; jet brakes

steps.title: Docking without a cut
steps.text: No more cut to a hangar far away: the pad's lift carries your ship 60 m down its shaft into the port under the platform, the shutters sliding shut over you once you're below the deck. Undocking, they open and the lift brings you up. Traders do the same - set down, ride their lift into the hall, unload, rise and fly on.

steps.title: The port: hall, concourse, rooms
steps.text: Under each platform hangs a port: its hall where the lifts come down (pillars by empire, frieze, banners, crates, a gantry crane), a concourse with windows onto the ships, and a row of rooms with windows out to space - the services hall with its terminals, the bar, the lounge, the harbour office, the stores.

steps.title: Its people
steps.text: The port's people are the empire's own: dock workers, two carrying crates in both hands, guards at the doors, clerks at the terminals, a bartender, spacers at the bar on stools, officers at their desks, travellers in the lounge and walking room to room. E to talk: who they are, the sector's news, and work - a mission you can accept on the spot. Sit down yourself at any free seat.

steps.title: Each service its own panel
steps.text: A terminal opens only its own service - the market, outfitting, the shipyard, the designer, reputation, missions, repairs, salvage - with no tabs to the others: one place for each. The rooms are furnished properly: chairs, armchairs, bar stools with foot rings, pedestal tables and desks in wood, upholstery in the empire's colour; all of it solid to walk round.

steps.title: The stations' law
steps.text: Every station is armed: eight heavy turrets at its platforms' corners. Fire on a trader or a patrol near a station and you're fined 250 dr - what you can't pay you owe, and no pad till it's paid. Destroy one, or fire on a station you're not at war with, and you're wanted in that system: its guns open fire on you, its patrols hunt you.

steps.title: War at the stations
steps.text: An invasion fleet besieging your system is there in ships: its warships circle the station they besiege and fire on it, and the station's guns answer. A station worn down burns. Come near one in trouble and it hails you: its defence and repair jobs, well paid, to accept there and then. Each warship you destroy counts for your missions and against its fleet.

steps.title: Worlds and people
steps.text: Each empire's planets lean toward its own palette - Minoa's turquoise seas, Sparta's rust and khaki, the Cyclades' white rock and aquamarine, the Sea Peoples' ash. The people are weathered - grime low down, dust, chipped paint, scratches - and the android's apron, heads and cape no longer pass through the body.

diagram.label:
heads and capes
clear of limbs

steps.title: Insides follow outsides
steps.text: A port's rooms are inside its own module, hung under its platform - nothing of the station passes through them, the lift shafts are clear, and there is open space outside every window. Sparta's corner towers stood where its platforms stand; its platforms now stand out from them, and every port stands clear of its ring. Your ship's rooms sit inside its hull all along.

review.intro: Patch 0018: the stations come alive - the ports under their platforms (the lift instead of a cut, the hall, the rooms, the people, sitting and carrying), each service its own panel, the stations' law and guns, sieges and hails; every empire its own people, ships, stations and towns; the jet pack to space and its finish; worlds in their empires' colours, weathered people, cloth and limbs clear of the body and the seats; insides that follow their outsides.

Its **people** walk its streets, each empire its own: the Minoans' **palace guards** (terracotta ceramic, a painted fan crest, laser rifles) and **androids** in a triceratops's image - a great painted frill, long brow horns, a red cape - armed with a **laser rifle**, a **laser bow** or a **labrys**, the Minoan double axe; Athens' horned, owl-eyed machines in marble and navy; Sparta's crested tyrants in iron and crimson; Mycenae's gold-domed masks; Ionia's lapis duck-bills with their long gold crests; the Cyclades' pale idols. They turn to look at you - and take on the pirates and hunting beasts that come near. **Kilon Alios**, the hooded wanderer who keeps the worlds for Ephestos, waits by every city's landing field: **E** beside him to talk - ask who he is, who you are, where you are, what your mission is, what you should become - and he offers you the main quest. Every town has a **landing field** beside it; from orbit the towns of the planet you're near are on your screen - **T** targets one, the Hyperion drive takes you there. Climb the stairs and walk the roofs. **Walk in**: every building has its doorway - the palace's wings open onto the court, their rooms one through another (the **throne room** in the west wing), stairs up to the upper floors; the houses have their hearths, benches, jars and beds upstairs. Indoors a warm light goes with you.
 
 ![](shot:space3d_inside)
 - **Pirate camps** - a tent, crates and a mast with a red light: their guards, pirate androids, open fire when you come near.

Each empire's towns and stations are now peopled by their own android instead of a recoloured Minoan one.

hunks.title: The Athenian android skin
hunks.note: Overrides the shared material keys with Athens's colours, defines its painted marks and builds its own head on the shared body.

bubbles.text: The laurel wreath: ten leaf patches set round an arc open at the top, with an owl's eyes and beak painted inside it - all laid proud of whatever surface it is given.
After the head's parts are made, they are scaled up and moved higher and further back on the neck, so the fists in the fighting clips no longer pass through the jaw and horns.
Mn.style plugs this skin's marks into the shared body: the body calls them wherever a pauldron, thigh, apron, back, chest or buckle mark goes.

files.explanation: Your automaton and the shared frame the pirate and Kilon wear. The frame was reshaped after its reference sheets (broad wedge pauldrons, a breastplate in two halves, flared greaves), the helmet rebuilt with slanted lights behind dark glass, and the rifle given more parts. It also gained general makers every skin uses - skin (a surface through rings of points), drape (a hanging cloth panel) and cable (a hose along a curve) - for coats, hoods, hat brims and hoses.

hunks.title: New makers; the frame and helmet rebuilt
hunks.note: Adds skin, drape and cable surface makers for every skin, then rebuilds the legs, body, helmet and arms with lofted plates and cheaper decals. The arm is split into pauldron, upper arm, forearm and hand functions so other skins can swap single pieces.

bubbles.at: def skin(name, rings, mat="armor", closed=True, caps=False, thick=0.0, smooth=True, split=0.0, skip=(), lining=None, inside=None):
bubbles.text: Joins rings of points into quads (a tube or a sheet), drops unused vertices, flips the normals away from an inside point, and can give the surface thickness with a lining material on its back.

bubbles.at: def drape(name, a0, a1, top, hem, mat="coat", cols=10, rows=6, thick=0.014, pleat=0.0, waves=3.0, phase=0.0, flare=1.3,
bubbles.text: A hanging cloth panel: an arc round the body from the top ring to the hem, with pleats, waves and flare, built with skin().
A decal cut twice instead of three times, so a mark on a curved plate costs 16 triangles per triangle instead of 64.
The pauldron is now its own function (a broad lofted shell with a rim), so a skin can replace it without rebuilding the whole arm.

hunks.title: The rifle gets more detail
hunks.note: The automaton's rifle is rebuilt: a lower receiver and trigger guard, a rail, vents, a barrel shroud, a muzzle band and a two-mount scope.

bubbles.text: Each part is a box placed by at(fwd, up), measured from the grip, so the rifle stays on the gun bone wherever the hands hold it.
A tapered sleeve over the barrel's root: two radii give the tube its taper.

files.explanation: A new skin: the Cycladic android. The Minoan android's body in the Cyclades' colours - near-white marble, thin blue and terracotta lines, a teal glow - with a smooth abstract head (an idol crossed with an ichthyosaur, a long toothed snout and a single dark fin) and a simple spiral as its mark.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,111 @@ 
+"""The Cycladic android: the Minoan android's build (minoan.py) in the
+Cyclades' colours - pure white marble, its panels barely a shade off it, thin
+lines of blue and terracotta, a teal glow - under its own head: smooth, pale
+and abstract, a Cycladic idol crossed with an ichthyosaur - a long smooth
+snout with rows of small teeth, a nose ridge like an idol's, tiny teal eyes,
+thin painted bands, and one flat dark fin standing on top of the skull. Its
+mark: a simple spiral. A laser rifle, no cape."""
+import kit
+import minoan as Mn
+from kit import bone, mirror
+
+GUN_HAND_R = Mn.GUN_HAND_R
+GUN_HAND_L = Mn.GUN_HAND_L
+
+
+def materials():
+    Mn.materials()
+    kit.M.update({
+        "armor": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Armor", "#f7f6f2", shade=0.62, hi=0.06),
+        "armor2": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Armor2", "#e7e6e1", shade=0.64),
+        "joint": kit.mat_toon("CYC_Joint", "#2f2d38", shade=0.62),
+        "grey": kit.mat_toon("CYC_LineBlue", "#3f86c9", shade=0.64),
+        "red": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Red", "#dedfdb", shade=0.68, hi=0.05),
+        "red2": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Red2", "#c6c9c8", shade=0.7),
+        "glow": kit.mat_glow("AUT_Glow", "#2fd6c4", 1.7),
+        "glow_y": kit.mat_glow("AUT_GlowY", "#b8fff4", 1.8),
+        "gold": kit.mat_toon("CYC_LineTerra", "#c8683f", shade=0.66),
+        "claw": kit.mat_toon("CYC_ClawBone", "#dcdad2", shade=0.62),
+        "cloth": kit.mat_toon("CYC_Cloth", "#f8f7f3", shade=0.66),
+        "marble": kit.mat_toon("CYC_MarbleSkin", "#f4f2eb", shade=0.64),
+        "marble2": kit.mat_toon("CYC_MarbleSkin2", "#e6e3da", shade=0.66),
+        "fin": kit.mat_toon("CYC_FinHide", "#262b34", shade=0.64),
+        "tooth": kit.mat_toon("CYC_ToothBone", "#fbf9f2", shade=0.64),
+        "eye": kit.mat_glow("CYC_EyeGlow", "#30e0cc", 1.9),
+        "rifle": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleBody", "#f2f1ec", shade=0.64, hi=0.08),
+        "rifle_d": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleDark", "#3a3f4c", shade=0.62, hi=0.1),
+        "rifle_t": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleGold", "#3f86c9", shade=0.66, hi=0.15),
+        "rifle_g": kit.mat_glow("MIN_RifleGlow", "#4fe8d6", 1.8),
+    })
+    Mn.paints("grey", "gold")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- its mark: a spiral, thinly drawn
+
+def m_thin(surf, r, mat="paint", hand=1.0, lift=0.004, walls=True):
+    Mn.stroke("Spiral", Mn.spiral_path(r * 0.06, r * 0.92, 2.25, n=22, hand=hand, a0=3.14159), 0.085 * r, surf, mat, lift=lift, walls=walls)
+
+
+def pauldron_mark(at, axis, r, sx):
+    m_thin(Mn.roundel("PauldronDisc", at, axis, r, [(0.9, 0), (1.0, 1)], ["armor", "gold"]), r * 0.8, hand=sx)
+
+
+def thigh_mark(at, axis, r, sx):
+    m_thin(Mn.roundel("ThighDisc", at, axis, r, [(0.9, 0), (1.0, 1)], ["armor", "paint"], h=0.012, seg=14), r * 0.78, "gold", hand=sx)
+
+
+def apron_mark(surf, r):
+    m_thin(surf, r * 0.75)
+    for v, mat in ((0.98, "gold"), (-0.98, "gold"), (-1.12, "paint")):
+        Mn.stroke("ApronThin", [(-0.8 * r, v * r), (0.8 * r, v * r)], 0.05 * r, surf, mat, lift=0.004, walls=False)
+
+
+def pec_mark(surf, r, sx):
+    Mn.stroke("PecMark", [(-r, 0), (r, 0)], 0.22 * r, surf, "paint", lift=0.004, walls=False)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the head: an idol's, an ichthyosaur's
+
+def head():
+    bone("head")
+    Mn.neck()
+    st = [(0.1, 0.07, 1.86, 1.70), (0.02, 0.086, 1.888, 1.69), (-0.08, 0.08, 1.878, 1.698), (-0.2, 0.058, 1.846, 1.71),
+          (-0.32, 0.04, 1.812, 1.722), (-0.42, 0.027, 1.786, 1.734), (-0.5, 0.017, 1.768, 1.744)]
+    Mn.hull("Skull", st, "marble", n=2.4, cap=0.8)
+    jaw = [(0.04, 0.072, 1.702, 1.648), (-0.08, 0.07, 1.702, 1.645), (-0.2, 0.05, 1.713, 1.668), (-0.32, 0.034, 1.724, 1.69),
+           (-0.42, 0.022, 1.735, 1.71), (-0.49, 0.014, 1.745, 1.728)]
+    Mn.hull("Jaw", jaw, "marble2", n=2.4, seg=16, cap=0.8)
+    ys = [-0.15 - 0.026 * k for k in range(13)]
+    Mn.jaw_teeth("Teeth", st, ys, [0.013 - 0.0004 * k for k in range(13)], inset=0.9, drop=0.004)
+    Mn.jaw_teeth("TeethLow", jaw, [y - 0.013 for y in ys[:12]], 0.009, inset=0.98, up=True, drop=0.003)
+    # the idol's nose: a ridge down the snout
+    Mn.sweep("NoseRidge", [(0, s[0], s[2]) for s in st[2:]], [(0.007, 0.011), (0.007, 0.01), (0.006, 0.008), (0.005, 0.006), (0.004, 0.004)],
+             mat="marble", seg=8, tip=False)
+    # thin painted bands round the snout
+    for y, mat in ((-0.235, "paint"), (-0.252, "gold"), (-0.38, "paint")):
+        a = Mn.at_y(st, y)
+        b = Mn.at_y(st, y - 0.008)
+        Mn.hull("SnoutBand", [(y, a[0] + 0.002, a[1] + 0.002, a[2] + 0.001), (y - 0.008, b[0] + 0.002, b[1] + 0.002, b[2] + 0.001)], mat, n=2.4,
+                seg=16, cap=0.0)
+    # the fin: flat and dark, standing on the skull, swept back
+    Mn.slab("Fin", [(0.075, 1.868), (0.045, 1.93), (-0.005, 1.99), (-0.065, 2.04), (-0.125, 2.062), (-0.108, 2.0), (-0.098, 1.93),
+                    (-0.095, 1.86)], (0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, -1, 0), thick=0.016, mat="fin", bevel=0.006)
+    Mn.slab("FinFoot", [(0.09, 1.862), (0.08, 1.884), (-0.1, 1.884), (-0.108, 1.855)], (0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, -1, 0), thick=0.03,
+            mat="marble2", bevel=0.008)
+    for sx in (1.0, -1.0):
+        Mn.lathe("Eye", (0.0765 * sx, -0.105, 1.802), (sx, -0.22, 0.1), [(0, 0.005, 1), (0.008, 0.003, 1), (0.01, 0.004, 0), (0.014, 0.004, 0),
+                                                                        (0.016, -0.006, 0)], ["joint", "eye"], seg=10)
+        Mn.stroke("CheekSpiral", Mn.spiral_path(0.004, 0.032, 2.0, n=18, hand=sx, c=(0.0, 0.0)), 0.0045,
+                  Mn.flat((0.084 * sx, 0.01, 1.775), (sx, 0, 0)), "paint", lift=0.0035)
+    Mn.grow("head", 1.2, lift=0.052, tilt=-2, back=0.03)       # (high and back: clear of its fists in a guard)
+
+
+def build():
+    materials()
+    Mn.style(pauldron=pauldron_mark, thigh=thigh_mark, apron=apron_mark, back=lambda surf, r: m_thin(surf, r * 0.7, "gold"), pec=pec_mark,
+             buckle=lambda surf, r: m_thin(surf, r * 0.8, "armor"))
+    mirror(Mn.legs)
+    Mn.body()
+    head()
+    mirror(Mn.arms)
+    Mn.rifle()

bubbles.text: The shared 'gold' key is reused for a terracotta line colour, so every trim on the body takes the Cycladic look without code changes.
A painted spiral: a stroke along a spiral path, laid on a flat plane at the cheek a few millimetres proud of the surface.
The head is enlarged and carried higher and further back so it stays clear of the fists in a fighting guard.

files.explanation: A new skin: the Ionian android. The Minoan android's body in Ionia's colours - white marble, lapis-blue panels, gold trim, a blue glow - with a duck-billed head and a long golden hollow crest, and the volute (the Ionic capital's scroll) as its mark.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,122 @@ 
+"""The Ionian android: the Minoan android's build (minoan.py) in Ionia's
+colours - white marble plates over a dark frame, lapis-blue panels, gold
+trim, a blue glow - under its own head: a lapis hadrosaur, duck-billed (the
+bill tipped with gold), with a long golden hollow crest sweeping back over
+the neck, banded with lapis; a gold scroll on each cheek. Its mark: the
+volute, the Ionic capital's scroll, on the pauldrons, the apron and the
+buckle. A laser rifle, no cape."""
+import math
+
+import kit
+import minoan as Mn
+from kit import bone, mirror
+
+GUN_HAND_R = Mn.GUN_HAND_R
+GUN_HAND_L = Mn.GUN_HAND_L
+
+
+def materials():
+    Mn.materials()
+    kit.M.update({
+        "armor": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Armor", "#f3f2ee", shade=0.62, hi=0.06),
+        "armor2": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Armor2", "#d5d8de", shade=0.64),
+        "joint": kit.mat_toon("ION_Joint", "#2b2a3a", shade=0.62),
+        "grey": kit.mat_toon("ION_Blue", "#4173d6", shade=0.64),
+        "red": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Red", "#2243b0", shade=0.68, hi=0.05),
+        "red2": kit.mat_toon("AUT_Red2", "#162c78", shade=0.7),
+        "glow": kit.mat_glow("AUT_Glow", "#3d9bff", 1.7),
+        "glow_y": kit.mat_glow("AUT_GlowY", "#bfe0ff", 1.8),
+        "gold": kit.mat_toon("ION_Gold", "#e9bb3e", shade=0.66, hi=0.15),
+        "claw": kit.mat_toon("ION_ClawGold", "#dcae36", shade=0.62, hi=0.1),
+        "cloth": kit.mat_toon("ION_Cloth", "#f5f3ef", shade=0.66),
+        "head": kit.mat_toon("ION_LapisArmor", "#2747b2", shade=0.64, hi=0.08),
+        "head2": kit.mat_toon("ION_LapisArmor2", "#1b3384", shade=0.66, hi=0.08),
+        "tube": kit.mat_toon("ION_TubeGold", "#ecc040", shade=0.66, hi=0.15),
+        "eye": kit.mat_glow("ION_EyeGlow", "#ffe27a", 1.8),
+        "rifle": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleBody", "#eeeeea", shade=0.64, hi=0.08),
+        "rifle_d": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleDark", "#1f3a9a", shade=0.62, hi=0.1),
+        "rifle_t": kit.mat_toon("MIN_RifleGold", "#e9bb3e", shade=0.66, hi=0.15),
+        "rifle_g": kit.mat_glow("MIN_RifleGlow", "#5ab0ff", 1.8),
+    })
+    Mn.paints("grey", "gold")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- its mark
+
+def m_volute(surf, r, mat="gold", lift=0.005, walls=True):
+    """The Ionic capital's scroll: two spirals joined by a band, the abacus over them."""
+    a0 = math.radians(90.0) - 1.6 * math.tau
+    left = Mn.spiral_path(0.06 * r, 0.4 * r, 1.6, n=14, hand=-1.0, a0=a0, c=(-0.5 * r, -0.12 * r))
+    right = Mn.spiral_path(0.06 * r, 0.4 * r, 1.6, n=14, hand=1.0, a0=a0, c=(0.5 * r, -0.12 * r))
+    Mn.stroke("Volute", left + right[::-1], 0.13 * r, surf, mat, lift=lift, walls=walls)
+    Mn.stroke("VoluteAbacus", [(-0.82 * r, 0.52 * r), (0.82 * r, 0.52 * r)], 0.13 * r, surf, mat, lift=lift, walls=walls)
+    for s in (1.0, -1.0):
+        Mn.patch("VoluteEye", Mn.circle(0.09 * r, 8, (0.5 * r * s, -0.12 * r)), surf, mat, lift=lift, walls=walls)
+
+
+def pauldron_mark(at, axis, r, sx):
+    m_volute(Mn.roundel("PauldronDisc", at, axis, r, [(0.86, 0), (1.0, 1)], ["red", "gold"]), r * 0.74)
+
+
+def thigh_mark(at, axis, r, sx):
+    Mn.m_spiral(Mn.roundel("ThighDisc", at, axis, r, [(0.84, 0), (1.0, 1)], ["armor2", "gold"], h=0.012, seg=14), r * 0.8, "red", hand=sx)
+
+
+def apron_mark(surf, r):
+    """A column's head: the volute, the fluted shaft under it."""
+    m_volute(lambda u, v: surf(u, v + 0.42 * r), r * 0.8, "red")
+    for k in range(4):
+        u = (k - 1.5) * 0.3 * r
+        Mn.stroke("Flute", [(u, 0.12 * r), (u, -0.95 * r)], 0.12 * r, surf, "paint" if k % 2 else "red", lift=0.004, walls=False)
+
+
+def pec_mark(surf, r, sx):
+    Mn.m_spiral(surf, r, "gold", hand=sx, lift=0.004, walls=False)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the head: a hadrosaur, its long hollow crest
+
+def head():
+    bone("head")
+    Mn.neck()
+    st = [(0.09, 0.074, 1.855, 1.70), (0.01, 0.092, 1.88, 1.69), (-0.08, 0.088, 1.868, 1.698), (-0.17, 0.072, 1.836, 1.704),
+          (-0.26, 0.058, 1.8, 1.71), (-0.33, 0.058, 1.77, 1.714, 3.4), (-0.385, 0.064, 1.752, 1.718, 3.6), (-0.415, 0.056, 1.744, 1.722, 3.6)]
+    Mn.hull("Skull", st, "head", n=2.8)
+    Mn.hull("Bill", [(-0.33, 0.06, 1.772, 1.713, 3.4), (-0.385, 0.068, 1.755, 1.716, 3.6), (-0.422, 0.059, 1.746, 1.72, 3.6)], "tube", seg=16,
+            cap=0.6)
+    jaw = [(0.04, 0.078, 1.702, 1.642), (-0.08, 0.078, 1.702, 1.636), (-0.2, 0.06, 1.708, 1.65), (-0.32, 0.052, 1.716, 1.674, 3.4),
+           (-0.4, 0.055, 1.722, 1.692, 3.6)]
+    Mn.hull("Jaw", jaw, "head2", n=2.8, seg=16)
+    Mn.hull("JawBill", [(-0.335, 0.054, 1.718, 1.676, 3.4), (-0.405, 0.058, 1.723, 1.69, 3.6)], "tube", seg=16, cap=0.5)
+    # the crest: a long hollow tube of gold, out of the snout's line, back over the head and the neck; lapis bands round it
+    path = [(0, -0.2, 1.812), (0, -0.12, 1.86), (0, -0.03, 1.905), (0, 0.07, 1.95), (0, 0.17, 1.99), (0, 0.27, 2.024), (0, 0.36, 2.05),
+            (0, 0.42, 2.063)]
+    rad = [(0.02, 0.03), (0.036, 0.038), (0.044, 0.04), (0.045, 0.038), (0.043, 0.035), (0.039, 0.032), (0.034, 0.028), (0.025, 0.021)]
+    Mn.sweep("Crest", path, rad, mat="tube", seg=12, tip=False)
+    Mn.sweep("CrestEnd", [path[-1], (0, 0.44, 2.067)], [rad[-1], (0.01, 0.009)], mat="tube", seg=12, tip=False)
+    for i in (3, 5):
+        p0, p1 = Mn.Vector(path[i]), Mn.Vector(path[i + 1])
+        Mn.sweep("CrestBand", [p0 + (p1 - p0) * 0.3, p0 + (p1 - p0) * 0.6], [(rad[i][0] + 0.004, rad[i][1] + 0.004)] * 2, mat="head",
+                 seg=12, tip=False)
+    # the struts holding it over the neck
+    Mn.sweep("CrestStrut", [(0, 0.07, 1.85), (0, 0.13, 1.96)], [(0.012, 0.016), (0.01, 0.012)], mat="head2", seg=6, tip=False)
+    for sx in (1.0, -1.0):
+        Mn.lathe("Eye", (0.088 * sx, -0.115, 1.806), (sx, -0.35, 0.08),
+                 [(0, 0.007, 1), (0.014, 0.004, 1), (0.016, 0.008, 0), (0.022, 0.008, 0), (0.026, -0.01, 0)], ["tube", "eye"], seg=12)
+        Mn.loft("Brow", (0.084 * sx, -0.05, 1.848), (0.074 * sx, -0.18, 1.826), [(0, 0.02, 0.013, 3), (1, 0.013, 0.009, 3)], mat="head2",
+                front=(sx, 0, 0.6), seg=8, cap=0.4)
+        Mn.lathe("Nostril", (0.03 * sx, -0.36, 1.764), (0.4 * sx, -0.3, 1), [(0, 0.002), (0.008, 0.002), (0.01, -0.004)], ["joint"], seg=8)
+        # the scroll on the cheek
+        Mn.m_spiral(Mn.flat((0.0935 * sx, 0.0, 1.772), (sx, 0, 0)), 0.042, "tube", hand=sx, lift=0.004, name="CheekScroll")
+    Mn.grow("head", 1.18, lift=0.052, tilt=-4, back=0.04)      # (high and back: clear of its fists in a guard)
+
+
+def build():
+    materials()
+    Mn.style(pauldron=pauldron_mark, thigh=thigh_mark, apron=apron_mark, back=lambda surf, r: m_volute(surf, r * 0.8, "red"), pec=pec_mark,
+             buckle=lambda surf, r: m_volute(surf, r * 0.85, "red"))
+    mirror(Mn.legs)
+    Mn.body()
+    head()
+    mirror(Mn.arms)
+    Mn.rifle()

files.explanation: Kilon Alios, the hooded wanderer, rebuilt after his reference sheet: a deep pointed hood made of arches, a long indigo coat open in front with lapels, sleeves, a belt with crossed straps and pockets, steel pauldrons and gauntlets. His coat tails now also have seated poses, so they lie clear of a chair or stool.

files.explanation: The shared rig, pose solver and part makers. This patch teaches it about seats: a pose can say it is on the game's chair or bar stool, the seats' shapes are described as collision boxes for the cloth to keep clear of, and a helper turns a skin's table of seated cloth poses into bone matrices. Cloth bones may now also be scaled (gathered up), and that scale is applied and keyframed.

hunks.note: Poses gain a 'seat' value; seated_cloth reads a skin's table to pose a cloth bone on a seat; SEATS describes the chair and stool as boxes matching the game's furniture.

bubbles.text: The default pose is not seated; the sit and stool clips set this to "sit" or "stool" so the tail solvers know where the furniture is.

Looks up the bone in the table for the current seat; if found, it turns the bone about its head by yaw, pitch and roll (mirrored for the right side), square to the pelvis, and scales it by length and width.
The sitter's origin sits 2 cm behind the seat's middle, so the proxies are offset by that much.
The chair's back is split into posts, a padded panel and a top rail, leaving the gap under the panel open for a coat tail to pass through.

files.explanation: The Minoan android, now a body of its own that every empire's android shares (the guard and the Athenian, Spartan, Mycenaean, Ionian and Cycladic skins). It brings its own part makers (slab, sweep, lathe, hull, painted strokes and patches), a style table each skin fills with its marks, a big beaked head with a scalloped frill, layered chest plates, round pauldrons, a meander belt and an apron split down the middle that follows the thighs. Its cape has its own solver: it swings clear of the legs when running and folds over a chair's back when seated.

hunks.title: Shared body; a cape solver that knows seats
hunks.note: The docstring explains the shared body and its makers; the cape gets its own tail solver instead of the pirate's, with constants for how it clears the legs and how it folds over a chair.

bubbles.text: On a chair the cape's bone is moved to just above the chair's top rail and swung back 24 degrees, so it hangs behind the chair's back.

bubbles.at: if seat == "sit":                       # (over the chair's back: kit.SEATS)
bubbles.text: Seated, the cape ignores the legs and is placed from the chair's rail box in kit.SEATS.
Standing or moving, the cape swings back far enough to clear every knee, shin and heel point below it by CAPE_CLEAR.
When the body tips over (lying or flipping) the cape blends toward simply following the chest.

+    if p.y < 0.0:
+        t = _smooth(APRON_FRONT[0], APRON_FRONT[1], p.z)
+    else:
+        t = _smooth(APRON_TOP, APRON_LOW, p.z)
+    s = 1.0 if p.x > 0.0 else 0.0
+    return 1.0 - t, t * s, t * (1.0 - s)

+def _fold_apron():
+    """The apron's parts cut across into rows and columns (so they bend where the
+    weights change); each vertex's weights, by its place at rest."""
+    w = {}
+    for ob in APRON:
+        if ob.name not in bpy.data.objects or ob.type != "MESH":
+            continue
+        mw = ob.matrix_world
+        inv = mw.inverted()
+        nm = mw.to_3x3().transposed()
+        bm = bmesh.new()
+        bm.from_mesh(ob.data)
+        for axis, cuts in ((2, APRON_CUTS[0]), (0, APRON_CUTS[1])):
+            d = Vector((0, 0, 0))
+            d[axis] = 1.0
+            for c in cuts:
+                pt = Vector((0, 0, 0))
+                pt[axis] = c
+                bmesh.ops.bisect_plane(bm, geom=bm.verts[:] + bm.edges[:] + bm.faces[:], dist=1e-5, plane_co=inv @ pt,
+                                       plane_no=(nm @ d).normalized())
+        # split down the middle: the cut's vertices doubled, each copy a hair toward its own half
+        mid = [e for e in bm.edges if all(abs((mw @ v.co).x) < 1e-5 for v in e.verts)]
+        if mid:
+            bmesh.ops.split_edges(bm, edges=mid)
+        for v in bm.verts:
+            p = mw @ v.co
+            if abs(p.x) < 1e-5 and v.link_faces:
+                side = sum((mw @ f.calc_center_median()).x for f in v.link_faces)
+                v.co = inv @ (p + Vector((APRON_GAP if side > 0 else -APRON_GAP, 0, 0)))

+        bm.free()
+        for v in ob.data.vertices:
+            p = mw @ v.co
+            w[_key(p)] = apron_weights(p)

A new skin: the Spartan android. The Minoan android's body in Sparta's colours - crimson and cream plates over a dark iron frame, gold trim, an amber glow - with a bronze tyrannosaur head, cheek guards like a helmet's, a tall red crest running front to back, and the gold lambda as its mark.

+colours - crimson plates and cream ones over a dark iron frame, gold trim, an
+amber glow - under its own head: a bronze tyrannosaur, heavy-jawed and
+toothed, orange eyes under brow bosses, cheek guards like a helmet's, and a
+tall red crest running front to back like a Spartan helmet's plume. Its mark:
+the gold lambda, on the pauldrons, the apron and the buckle. A laser rifle,
+no cape."""

Before, every empire's town was built the Minoan way with another palette; now the Builder knows whose town it is and builds that empire's own architecture: Doric, Ionic or square columns, tiled gable roofs with pediments, bronze shields, gold bands, domes, a relieving triangle over Mycenaean doors, each empire's own shrine (temple, tholos, domed chapel) and altar ornament. files.explanation: CosmosWarm runs at the title screen and draws one of every kind of 3D material off screen so its shaders and pipelines are compiled before the game needs them. To keep starting a game within the frame-time bar it now also loads the first game's scripts and scenes and every character model on background threads, adds a point and a spot light so pipelines for lit scenes are built too, warms the new empire look (on a mesh carrying its zone colours and UVs, plus MultiMesh instances), the jet pack's dust and heat haze, the port's glass, the HUD's real theme font and 3D labels - and keeps all those materials (and the labels) alive for the run, since Godot drops a standard material's shader when the last material using it is freed.

files.explanation: New file. EmpireHulls designs every empire's NPC ships - small ones (patrols, fighters, raiders) and big ones (traders), two variants each - from the empires' reference sheets: Athens' marble scythe wings and temple-carrying traders, Sparta's lambda shield and gun barrels, the Minoan double-axe wings, Mycenae's tusks and gold dome, Ionia's column with volutes, the Cyclades' smooth marble with rib oars, the raiders' spikes and tattered sail, plain independents. Each design is one mesh (plus a glass mesh) built in unit space on a worker thread with EmpireKit's Mesher, cached and shared by every ship of that kind, scaled to the ship when placed; a ship is launched only once its design is ready, so nothing is built on the main thread.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,524 @@ 
+class_name EmpireHulls
+extends RefCounted
+## The empires' ships (the 3D game's other ships: traders, patrols, raiders),
+## each empire's from its reference sheet (external/images/<empire>_ships_1.png)
+## in its look (EmpireKit: colours, emblem, frieze):
+##   Athens - marble and navy, scythe wings curving forward, the owl; the big
+##     ones carry a temple's colonnade;
+##   Sparta - an iron frame under cream and crimson plates, the lambda on an
+##     eight-sided shield, swept wings, guns along its sides;
+##   Minoa - cream and red, twin prow horns, the double axe's blades for wings
+##     (its haulers: your ship's kind - MinoanShip);
+##   Mycenae - blocks of stone banded in gold, boar's tusks at the bow, a gold
+##     dome with the rosette;
+##   Ionia - marble and lapis, an Ionic column across the hull, volutes at the
+##     tips of its curling wings;
+##   the Cyclades - one smooth piece of white marble, a curled prow, oars of
+##     ribs, the spiral;
+##   the Sea Peoples - dark iron and red, scythes, bone spikes, a tattered sail,
+##     the skull; and the independents' plain grey hulls.
+## A design is small ("fighter", "patrol", "pirate") or big (the traders), in
+## two variants; each is one mesh (+ its glass), made on a worker (`warm`),
+## shared by every ship of its kind and scaled to the ship. Built in unit
+## space - the nose at z -1, the nozzles at +1 - then to its nominal size.
+
+const SMALL := 13.0            # the nominal half length (m) a design's seams and marks are made for
+const BIG := 40.0
+const VARIANTS := 2
+
+static var _cache := {}        # key -> {task, out: [arrays...], mesh, glass}
+
+
+static func _key(emp: String, big: bool, v: int) -> String:
+	return "%s|%d|%d" % [emp, int(big), v]
+
+
+static func _emp(empire: String) -> String:
+	return empire if EmpireKit.LOOKS.has(empire) else ""
+
+
+## Starts the builds of an empire's ships (and the raiders', the independents') on workers.
+static func warm(empires: Array) -> void:
+	for e in empires:
+		var emp := _emp(str(e))
+		for big in [false, true]:
+			if big and emp == Galaxy.HOME_EMPIRE:
+				continue   # (the Minoan haulers: MinoanShip)
+			for v in VARIANTS:
+				_start(emp, big, v)
+
+
+static func _start(emp: String, big: bool, v: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var k := _key(emp, big, v)
+	if _cache.has(k):
+		return _cache[k]
+	var entry := {"task": -1, "out": [], "mesh": null, "glass": null}
+	_cache[k] = entry
+	var out: Array = entry["out"]
+	entry["task"] = WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func(): out.append_array(build(emp, big, v)), false, "ship design")
+	return entry
+
+
+static func _meshes(emp: String, big: bool, v: int) -> Array:
+	var e := _start(emp, big, v)
+	if int(e["task"]) >= 0:
+		WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(int(e["task"]))
+		e["task"] = -1
+	if e["mesh"] == null:
+		var out: Array = e["out"]
+		var m := ArrayMesh.new()
+		m.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, out[0])
+		e["mesh"] = m
+		if not (out[1][Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array).is_empty():
+			var g := ArrayMesh.new()
+			g.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, out[1])
+			e["glass"] = g
+	return [e["mesh"], e["glass"]]
+
+
+## True once every design a ship of `empire` and `kind` could wear is made
+## (else their builds are started): a ship is launched when its hull is ready,
+## not waited for.
+static func ready(empire: String, kind: String) -> bool:
+	var emp := _emp(empire)
+	var big := kind in ["trader", "freighter", "hauler"]
+	var ok := true
+	for v in VARIANTS:
+		var e := _start(emp, big, v)
+		if int(e["task"]) >= 0 and not WorkerThreadPool.is_task_completed(int(e["task"])):
+			ok = false
+	return ok
+
+
+## Every build done (tests, leaving the game: no task left running).
+static func finish() -> void:
+	for k in _cache:
+		if int(_cache[k]["task"]) >= 0:
+			WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(int(_cache[k]["task"]))
+			_cache[k]["task"] = -1
+
+
+## A ship of `empire` ("pirates": a raider's) into `root`, `reach` its half
+## length (m): the nozzles' places, for their glows.
+static func place(root: Node3D, empire: String, kind: String, reach: float, seed: int) -> Array:
+	var emp := _emp(empire)
+	var big := kind in ["trader", "freighter", "hauler"]
+	var v := absi(seed) % VARIANTS
+	var ms := _meshes(emp, big, v)
+	var nominal := BIG if big else SMALL
+	var holder := Node3D.new()
+	holder.name = "Hull"
+	holder.scale = Vector3.ONE * (reach / nominal)
+	root.add_child(holder)
+	var body := MeshInstance3D.new()
+	body.name = "Body"
+	body.mesh = ms[0]
+	body.material_override = EmpireKit.mat("hull", emp)
+	holder.add_child(body)
+	if ms[1] != null:
+		var gl := MeshInstance3D.new()
+		gl.mesh = ms[1]
+		gl.material_override = EmpireKit.glass()
+		gl.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
+		holder.add_child(gl)
+	var out: Array = []
+	for e in engines(emp, big, v):
+		out.append(Vector3(e[0], e[1], 1.02) * reach)
+	return out
+
+
+## Where a design's engines are (unit space): [x, y, radius].
+static func engines(emp: String, big: bool, v: int) -> Array:
+	var r := 0.085 if big else 0.07
+	match emp:
+		"sparta", "pirates":
+			return [[-0.2, 0.0, r], [0.0, 0.02, r * 1.1], [0.2, 0.0, r]] if not big else [[-0.26, 0.0, r], [-0.09, 0.0, r], [0.09, 0.0, r], [0.26, 0.0, r]]
+		"cyclades":
+			return [[-0.11, -0.01, r * 0.8], [0.0, 0.03, r * 0.8], [0.11, -0.01, r * 0.8]]
+		"mycenae":
+			return [[-0.17, 0.0, r * 1.15], [0.17, 0.0, r * 1.15]] if not big else [[-0.24, 0.0, r * 1.1], [0.0, 0.0, r * 1.1], [0.24, 0.0, r * 1.1]]
+	if big:
+		return [[-0.24, 0.0, r], [0.0, 0.04, r], [0.24, 0.0, r]]
+	return [[-0.17, 0.0, r], [0.17, 0.0, r]] if v == 0 else [[-0.19, 0.0, r * 0.9], [0.0, 0.03, r * 0.9], [0.19, 0.0, r * 0.9]]
+
+
+# --- The builds ----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## [hull arrays, glass arrays] of a design, at its nominal size.
+static func build(emp: String, big: bool, v: int) -> Array:
+	var m := EmpireKit.Mesher.new()
+	var g := EmpireKit.Mesher.new()
+	match emp:
+		"athens": _athens(m, g, big, v)
+		"sparta": _sparta(m, g, big, v)
+		"minoa": _minoa(m, g, v)
+		"mycenae": _mycenae(m, g, big, v)
+		"ionia": _ionia(m, g, big, v)
+		"cyclades": _cyclades(m, g, big, v)
+		"pirates": _pirates(m, g, big, v)
+		_: _plain(m, g, big, v)
+	var zone := EmpireKit.MAIN if emp != "sparta" and emp != "pirates" else EmpireKit.IRON
+	for e in engines(emp, big, v):
+		_nacelle(m, e[0], e[1], e[2], zone)
+	var s := BIG if big else SMALL
+	var out := [m.arrays(), g.arrays()]
+	for a in out:
+		var vs: PackedVector3Array = a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]
+		for i in vs.size():
+			vs[i] *= s
+		a[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = vs
+	return out
+
+
+## An engine: a cowl from the hull's shoulder back to its nozzle (a band, a ring, the dark throat).
+static func _nacelle(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, x: float, y: float, r: float, zone: int) -> void:
+	m.lathe(x, y, [[0.42, 0.0, zone], [0.42, r * 0.55, zone], [0.52, r * 0.95, zone], [0.6, r, zone], [0.7, r, EmpireKit.ACCENT],
+		[0.72, r * 1.04, EmpireKit.GOLD], [0.76, r * 1.04, EmpireKit.GOLD], [0.76, r, zone], [0.9, r, zone], [0.9, r * 1.1, EmpireKit.STEEL],
+		[0.95, r * 1.1, EmpireKit.STEEL], [0.96, r * 1.02, EmpireKit.IRON], [1.02, r * 0.92, EmpireKit.IRON], [1.02, r * 0.74, EmpireKit.IRON],
+		[0.95, r * 0.4, EmpireKit.IRON], [0.95, 0.0, EmpireKit.LAMP]], 12)
+
+
+## The fuselage: [z, half width, top, bottom, chamfer] sections, the faces' zones by `zones`
+## [top, upper chamfers, sides, lower chamfers, bottom]; a band of `band` zone on the sides of segment `band_at`.
+static func _fuselage(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, secs: Array, zones: Array, band_at := -1, band := EmpireKit.ACCENT) -> void:
+	m.loft(secs, func(seg: int, f: int) -> int:
+		if seg == band_at and (f in EmpireKit.SIDES or f in EmpireKit.UPPER):
+			return band
+		if f == EmpireKit.TOP:
+			return zones[0]
+		if f in EmpireKit.UPPER:
+			return zones[1]
+		if f in EmpireKit.SIDES:
+			return zones[2]
+		if f in EmpireKit.LOWER:
+			return zones[3]
+		return zones[4])
+
+
+static func _secs(big: bool, w := 1.0, h := 1.0) -> Array:
+	if big:
+		return [[-1.0, 0.03 * w, 0.02 * h, -0.03 * h, 0.015], [-0.8, 0.12 * w, 0.08 * h, -0.08 * h, 0.05], [-0.45, 0.2 * w, 0.14 * h, -0.12 * h, 0.06],
+			[0.3, 0.22 * w, 0.15 * h, -0.13 * h, 0.06], [0.62, 0.2 * w, 0.13 * h, -0.12 * h, 0.06], [0.78, 0.15 * w, 0.1 * h, -0.09 * h, 0.05]]
+	return [[-1.0, 0.012 * w, 0.008 * h, -0.016 * h, 0.006], [-0.72, 0.065 * w, 0.045 * h, -0.045 * h, 0.028], [-0.3, 0.115 * w, 0.085 * h, -0.07 * h, 0.04],
+		[0.2, 0.135 * w, 0.095 * h, -0.08 * h, 0.042], [0.58, 0.12 * w, 0.085 * h, -0.07 * h, 0.04], [0.78, 0.09 * w, 0.065 * h, -0.055 * h, 0.03]]
+
+
+## The canopy: a blister of glass over the bow (dark under it), its frame.
+static func _canopy(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, g: EmpireKit.Mesher, z0: float, z1: float, w: float, y: float, h: float) -> void:
+	var secs := [[z0, w * 0.35, y + h * 0.25, y - 0.01, w * 0.2], [lerpf(z0, z1, 0.4), w, y + h, y - 0.01, w * 0.45], [z1, w * 0.7, y + h * 0.6, y - 0.01, w * 0.3]]
+	g.loft(secs, func(_s: int, _f: int) -> int: return 0)
+	m.boxat(Vector3(w * 1.5, 0.006, (z1 - z0) * 0.9), Vector3(0, y + 0.002, (z0 + z1) * 0.5), EmpireKit.IRON)
+	m.boxat(Vector3(w * 2.1, 0.012, 0.012), Vector3(0, y + h * 0.75, lerpf(z0, z1, 0.4)), EmpireKit.STEEL)
+
+
+## A band along an arc, from thick to a point (a scythe, a horn) or thick in
+## the middle (`sym`: a crescent, an axe's blade) - an outline for a slab.
+static func crescent(c: Vector2, r: float, a0: float, a1: float, t0: float, n := 12, pw := 0.8, sym := false) -> PackedVector2Array:
+	var outer: Array = []
+	var inner: Array = []
+	for i in n + 1:
+		var s := float(i) / n
+		var a := lerpf(a0, a1, s)
+		var t := t0 * (pow(sin(PI * s), pw) if sym else pow(1.0 - s, pw))
+		t = maxf(t, t0 * 0.02)
+		var d := Vector2(cos(a), sin(a))
+		outer.append(c + d * (r + t * 0.5))
+		inner.append(c + d * (r - t * 0.5))
+	inner.reverse()
+	return PackedVector2Array(outer + inner)
+
+
+## A wing each side: `pts` (x >= 0 out, y = z) mirrored, at height `y`, a dihedral, the face `zone`, the rim `edge`.
+static func _wings(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, pts: PackedVector2Array, y: float, t: float, zone: int, edge: int, dihedral := 0.0) -> void:
+	for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+		var q := PackedVector2Array()
+		for p in pts:
+			q.append(Vector2(p.x * sx, p.y))
+		m.slab(q, Transform3D(Basis(Vector3(0, 0, 1), dihedral * sx), Vector3(0, y, 0)), t, zone, edge)
+
+
+## The emblem: a disc on top of the hull, and one on each flank.
+static func _marks(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, z: float, top: float, r: float, side_x: float, side_r: float) -> void:
+	m.cyl(Vector3(0, top - 0.004, z), Vector3(0, top + 0.006, z), r * 1.08, r * 1.08, EmpireKit.GOLD, 24)
+	m.disc(Vector3(0, top + 0.0075, z), Vector3.UP, Vector3.FORWARD, r, EmpireKit.ROUNDEL, 28)
+	if side_r > 0.0:
+		for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+			m.disc(Vector3(sx * side_x, 0.0, z), Vector3(sx, 0, 0), Vector3.UP, side_r, EmpireKit.ROUNDEL, 20)
+
+
+## Lamps along the flanks.
+static func _lamps(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, secs: Array, from: float, to: float, n: int, y := -0.01) -> void:
+	for i in n:
+		var z := lerpf(from, to, (i + 0.5) / n)
+		var s := EmpireKit.section_at(secs, z)
+		for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+			m.boxat(Vector3(0.008, 0.012, (to - from) / n * 0.5), Vector3(sx * (float(s[1]) + 0.002), y, z), EmpireKit.LAMP)
+
+
+## Cargo modules along a big ship's flanks.
+static func _cargo(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, x: float, zone_a: int, zone_b: int, n := 3) -> void:
+	for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+		for k in n:
+			var z := -0.42 + k * 0.3
+			m.boxat(Vector3(0.12, 0.16, 0.26), Vector3(sx * x, -0.01, z), zone_a if k % 2 == 0 else zone_b)
+			m.boxat(Vector3(0.126, 0.166, 0.03), Vector3(sx * x, -0.01, z), EmpireKit.GOLD)   # (a band round its middle)
+			m.boxat(Vector3(0.008, 0.02, 0.18), Vector3(sx * (x + 0.062), -0.03, z), EmpireKit.LAMP)
+
+
+static func _athens(m: EmpireKit.Mesher, g: EmpireKit.Mesher, big: bool, v: int) -> void:
+	var secs := _secs(big)
+	_fuselage(m, secs, [EmpireKit.MAIN, EmpireKit.ACCENT, EmpireKit.MAIN, EmpireKit.MAIN, EmpireKit.IRON], 1, EmpireKit.GOLD)
+	var top: float = EmpireKit.section_at(secs, 0.1)[2]
+	if big:
+		# A temple amidships: its colonnade down both sides, the entablature, a navy roof.
+		var hw := 0.24
+		m.boxat(Vector3(hw * 2.0, 0.02, 0.72), Vector3(0, top + 0.01, 0.0), EmpireKit.MAIN)
+		m.boxat(Vector3(hw * 1.3, 0.11, 0.6), Vector3(0, top + 0.075, 0.0), EmpireKit.MAIN)
+		for sx in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+			for k in 7:

hunks.title: Ship designs for every empire
hunks.note: The whole new module: a build cache with worker tasks, readiness checks, placing a hull under a ship node, the engine layouts, the shared part builders (fuselage lofts, nacelles, canopies, crescent wings, emblems, lamps, cargo) and one design function per empire.

bubbles.at: entry["task"] = WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func(): out.append_array(build(emp, big, v)), false, "ship design")
bubbles.text: The design's vertex arrays are produced on a worker; the main thread later only wraps them in an ArrayMesh, which is cheap.

bubbles.at: static func ready(empire: String, kind: String) -> bool:
bubbles.text: Spawners ask this first: if either variant is still building, the ship simply launches a little later instead of the frame waiting.
One shared mesh per design serves every ship size: the holder node scales it from its nominal length to the ship's.

bubbles.at: static func crescent(c: Vector2, r: float, a0: float, a1: float, t0: float, n := 12, pw := 0.8, sym := false) -> PackedVector2Array:
bubbles.text: Builds a curved outline thick at one end tapering to a point (or thick in the middle) - cut into a slab it becomes a scythe wing, a horn or an axe blade.

files.explanation: New file, replacing minoan_kit.gd. EmpireKit generalises the Minoan look to every empire: LOOKS holds each empire's palette (main, accent, second accent, iron, steel, gold, lamps), its emblem and frieze numbers and their colours, how worn its paint is, and whether its stone is masonry or veined marble. mat() builds one shared ShaderMaterial per empire and kind (hull, inside, or the new station kind with larger plates, floodlit devices and swaying banners). The Mesher, which collects zone-coloured faces into one mesh, gains slabs cut to a 2D outline (wings, sails) and smooth round lofts; crates become two shared meshes for instancing.

+class_name EmpireKit
+extends RefCounted
+## The empires' looks for ships, stations and their insides, as parts merged
+## into one mesh a model (shaders/world/empire.gdshader: each face's zone -
+## paint, metal, lamp, screen, leather, cloth, the roundel, the banner, the
+## frieze - in its vertex colour). An empire is a material: its colours, its
+## emblem (the Minoan triskelion and bull, Athens' owl, Sparta's lambda,
+## Mycenae's rosette, Ionia's lyre, the Cyclades' spiral, the Sea Peoples'
+## skull) and its frieze - LOOKS, from the reference sheets
+## (external/images/<empire>_ships_1.png, _spacestations_1.png).
+## A Mesher collects faces (armoured lofts of chamfered sections, lathed
+## nacelles, boxes, discs, slabs cut to an outline, flat decals) and commits
+## them once; the materials are shared (`mat`: the hull, outside / inside, a
+## station's; `glass`; `zone_mat` for other builders' meshes). Builds are
+## plain data: worker threads make them.
+
+enum { MAIN, ACCENT, IRON, STEEL, LAMP, SCREEN, ROUNDEL, BANNER, LEATHER, CLOTH, LEAVES, HAZARD, FRIEZE, GOLD, ACCENT2, WOOD }
+
+const SHADER := preload("res://shaders/world/empire.gdshader")
+## An empire's look: its colours (main, accent, second accent, iron, steel,

+## marble, the seams' spacing on a ship (m).

+		"wear": 1.0, "blocks": 0.0, "marble": 0.0, "panel": 2.2},

+		"e_ground": Color(0.62, 0.08, 0.06), "e_ink": Color(0.85, 0.8, 0.66), "f_ground": Color(0.14, 0.14, 0.16), "f_ink": Color(0.85, 0.8, 0.66),
+		"wear": 1.5, "blocks": 0.0, "marble": 0.0, "panel": 1.8},
+	"": {"main": Color(0.70, 0.71, 0.73), "accent": Color(0.82, 0.42, 0.12), "accent2": Color(0.2, 0.3, 0.4), "iron": Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.22),
+		"steel": Color(0.6, 0.6, 0.62), "gold": Color(0.7, 0.6, 0.4), "lamp": Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.6), "emblem": 7, "frieze": 1,
+		"e_ground": Color(0.82, 0.42, 0.12), "e_ink": Color(0.9, 0.9, 0.9), "f_ground": Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.22), "f_ink": Color(0.82, 0.42, 0.12),
+		"wear": 1.0, "blocks": 0.0, "marble": 0.0, "panel": 2.2}}
+static var _mats := {}
+
+
+static func look(empire: String) -> Dictionary:
+	return LOOKS.get(empire, LOOKS[""])
+
+
+## An empire's material: "hull" (worn, outside), "inside" (cleaner, no mirror
+## metal) or "station" (a station's: plates the size of its scale).
+static func mat(kind := "hull", empire := "minoa") -> ShaderMaterial:
+	var key := kind + "|" + empire
+	if _mats.has(key):
+		return _mats[key]
+	var L := look(empire)
+	var m := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	m.shader = SHADER
+	m.set_shader_parameter("noise_tex", Cosmos.noise_ready())
+	for k in [["cream", "main"], ["red", "accent"], ["accent2", "accent2"], ["iron", "iron"], ["steel", "steel"], ["gold", "gold"],
+			["amber", "lamp"], ["emblem_ground", "e_ground"], ["emblem_ink", "e_ink"], ["frieze_ground", "f_ground"], ["frieze_ink", "f_ink"]]:
+		m.set_shader_parameter(k[0], L[k[1]])
+	m.set_shader_parameter("emblem", int(L["emblem"]))
+	m.set_shader_parameter("frieze", int(L["frieze"]))
+	m.set_shader_parameter("wear", float(L["wear"]))
+	m.set_shader_parameter("blocks", float(L["blocks"]))
+	m.set_shader_parameter("marble", float(L["marble"]))
+	m.set_shader_parameter("panel", float(L["panel"]))
+	if kind == "inside":
+		m.set_shader_parameter("wear", float(L["wear"]) * 0.35)
+		m.set_shader_parameter("inside", 1.0)
+		m.set_shader_parameter("sway", 0.18)   # (the air stirring the banners)
+	elif kind == "station":
+		m.set_shader_parameter("panel", float(L["panel"]) * 4.0)
+		m.set_shader_parameter("flood", 0.45)
+		m.set_shader_parameter("sway", 1.4)
+	_mats[key] = m
+	return m
+
+
+## A material that's one zone all over (for meshes without the zone colours).
+static func zone_mat(zone: int, kind := "hull", empire := "minoa") -> ShaderMaterial:
+	var key := "%s|%s:%d" % [kind, empire, zone]
+	if _mats.has(key):
+		return _mats[key]
+	var m := mat(kind, empire).duplicate() as ShaderMaterial
+	m.set_shader_parameter("zone_override", float(zone))
+	_mats[key] = m
+	return m
+
+
+## The windows: tinted, glossy, see-through (their outside only: from within you look out).
+static func glass() -> StandardMaterial3D:
+	if _mats.has("glass"):
+		return _mats["glass"]
+	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
+	m.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
+	m.albedo_color = Color(0.25, 0.32, 0.36, 0.28)
+	m.metallic = 0.6
+	m.roughness = 0.05
+	m.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_BACK
+	_mats["glass"] = m
+	return m
+
+
+## A soft additive glow (a hologram).
+static func holo() -> StandardMaterial3D:
+	if _mats.has("holo"):
+		return _mats["holo"]
+	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
+	m.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
+	m.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
+	m.blend_mode = BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_ADD
+	m.albedo_color = Color(0.25, 0.6, 1.0, 0.35)
+	m.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED
+	_mats["holo"] = m
+	return m
+
+
+## Faces gathered for one mesh.
+class Mesher:
+	var st := SurfaceTool.new()
+	var n := 0
+
+	func _init() -> void:
+		st.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
+
+	func _c(zone: int, g := 0.0) -> Color:
+		return Color(zone / 16.0, g, 0.0, 1.0)
+
+	## A triangle facing away from `inner` (a point inside the part).
+	func tri(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3, zone: int, inner: Vector3, uv := [Vector2.ZERO, Vector2.ZERO, Vector2.ZERO], g := 0.0) -> void:
+		var nrm := (b - a).cross(c - a)
+		if nrm.length_squared() < 1e-12:
+			return
+		nrm = nrm.normalized()
+		var pts := [a, b, c]
+		var uvs: Array = uv
+		if nrm.dot((a + b + c) / 3.0 - inner) < 0.0:
+			nrm = -nrm
+			pts = [a, c, b]
+			uvs = [uv[0], uv[2], uv[1]]
+		# (Godot's front faces wind clockwise seen from the front)
+		var col := _c(zone, g)
+		for k in [0, 2, 1]:
+			st.set_color(col)
+			st.set_normal(nrm)
+			st.set_uv(uvs[k])
+			st.add_vertex(pts[k])
+		n += 1
+
+	func quad(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3, d: Vector3, zone: int, inner: Vector3, g := 0.0) -> void:
+		var u := [Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(0, 1)]
+		tri(a, b, c, zone, inner, [u[0], u[1], u[2]], g)
+		tri(a, c, d, zone, inner, [u[0], u[2], u[3]], g)
+
+	## A raised plate on a face: the quad a b c d (on the face), lifted `h` off it, its edges closed.
+	func plate(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3, d: Vector3, h: float, zone: int, inner: Vector3) -> void:
+		var nrm := (b - a).cross(d - a).normalized()
+		if nrm.dot((a + c) * 0.5 - inner) < 0.0:
+			nrm = -nrm
+		var up := nrm * h
+		var mid := (a + b + c + d) * 0.25
+		quad(a + up, b + up, c + up, d + up, zone, mid - nrm)
+		var lo := [a, b, c, d]
+		for i in 4:
+			var j := (i + 1) % 4
+			quad(lo[i], lo[j], lo[j] + up, lo[i] + up, zone, mid + up * 0.5)
+
+	## A box (`size` full) placed by `xf`.
+	func box(size: Vector3, xf: Transform3D, zone: int) -> void:
+		var h := size * 0.5
+		var p := []
+		for i in 8:
+			p.append(xf * Vector3(h.x if i & 1 else -h.x, h.y if i & 2 else -h.y, h.z if i & 4 else -h.z))
+		var o := xf.origin
+		for f in [[0, 1, 3, 2], [4, 5, 7, 6], [0, 1, 5, 4], [2, 3, 7, 6], [0, 2, 6, 4], [1, 3, 7, 5]]:
+			quad(p[f[0]], p[f[1]], p[f[2]], p[f[3]], zone, o)
+
+	func boxat(size: Vector3, at: Vector3, zone: int, yaw := 0.0) -> void:
+		box(size, Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, yaw), at), zone)
+
+	## A flat panel (a decal, a screen, a banner): its middle, half extents along `right` and `down`.
+	func panel(mid: Vector3, right: Vector3, down: Vector3, zone: int, facing: Vector3, g := 0.0) -> void:
+		var a := mid - right - down
+		var b := mid + right - down
+		var c := mid + right + down
+		var d := mid - right + down
+		var inner := mid - facing
+		tri(a, b, c, zone, inner, [Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(1, 1)], g)
+		tri(a, c, d, zone, inner, [Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(0, 1)], g)
+
+	## A disc (a roundel): UV across it 0..1.
+	func disc(mid: Vector3, normal: Vector3, up: Vector3, r: float, zone: int, seg := 32) -> void:
+		var right := up.cross(normal).normalized() * r
+		var u2 := normal.cross(right).normalized() * r
+		for i in seg:
+			var a0 := TAU * i / seg
+			var a1 := TAU * (i + 1) / seg
+			var p0 := mid + right * cos(a0) + u2 * sin(a0)
+			var p1 := mid + right * cos(a1) + u2 * sin(a1)
+			tri(mid, p0, p1, zone, mid - normal, [Vector2(0.5, 0.5), Vector2(0.5 + 0.5 * cos(a0), 0.5 - 0.5 * sin(a0)), Vector2(0.5 + 0.5 * cos(a1), 0.5 - 0.5 * sin(a1))])
+
+	## A cylinder between `a` and `b` (radii ra, rb), `caps` closed.
+	func cyl(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, ra: float, rb: float, zone: int, seg := 12, caps := true) -> void:
+		if a.distance_squared_to(b) < 1e-8:
+			return
+		var ax := (b - a).normalized()
+		var side := ax.cross(Vector3.UP if absf(ax.y) < 0.9 else Vector3.RIGHT).normalized()
+		var up := ax.cross(side)
+		for i in seg:
+			var a0 := TAU * i / seg
+			var a1 := TAU * (i + 1) / seg
+			var d0 := side * cos(a0) + up * sin(a0)
+			var d1 := side * cos(a1) + up * sin(a1)
+			quad(a + d0 * ra, a + d1 * ra, b + d1 * rb, b + d0 * rb, zone, (a + b) * 0.5)
+			if caps:
+				tri(a, a + d0 * ra, a + d1 * ra, zone, a + ax)
+				tri(b, b + d1 * rb, b + d0 * rb, zone, b - ax)
+
+	## A lathe round the z axis through (x, y): profile [[z, r, zone], ...] - its
+	## faces outward on the profile's right (going on in z, away from the axis;
+	## a step in at one z faces back, out faces forward).
+	func lathe(x: float, y: float, prof: Array, seg := 16) -> void:
+		for k in prof.size() - 1:
+			var p0: Array = prof[k]
+			var p1: Array = prof[k + 1]
+			var dz := float(p1[0]) - float(p0[0])
+			var dr := float(p1[1]) - float(p0[1])
+			var nz := -dr
+			var nr := dz
+			var c0 := Vector3(x, y, p0[0])
+			var c1 := Vector3(x, y, p1[0])
+			for i in seg:
+				var a0 := TAU * (i + 0.5) / seg
+				var a1 := TAU * (i + 1.5) / seg
+				var d0 := Vector3(cos(a0), sin(a0), 0)
+				var d1 := Vector3(cos(a1), sin(a1), 0)
+				var q := [c0 + d0 * p0[1], c0 + d1 * p0[1], c1 + d1 * p1[1], c1 + d0 * p1[1]]
+				var mid: Vector3 = (q[0] + q[1] + q[2] + q[3]) * 0.25
+				var dm := Vector3(cos(TAU * (i + 1.0) / seg), sin(TAU * (i + 1.0) / seg), 0)
+				var out := (dm * nr + Vector3(0, 0, nz)).normalized()
+				quad(q[0], q[1], q[2], q[3], int(p1[2]), mid - out * 0.1)
+
+	## An armoured loft through chamfered sections [z, half width, top, bottom, chamfer]:
+	## eight faces round (top, chamfers, sides, bottom), `zone_of.call(segment, face)`
+	## the zone of each (-1: left out - glass goes in another mesh). `cap_front` closes the first.
+	func loft(sections: Array, zone_of: Callable, cap_front := true, cap_back := true) -> void:
+		var rings: Array = []
+		for s in sections:
+			rings.append(ring(s))
+		for k in sections.size() - 1:

+const UPPER := [1, 7]

+		m.disc(xf * Vector3(sx * (size.x * 0.5 + 0.012), 0, 0), nrm, Vector3.UP, r, ROUNDEL, 20)
hunks.title: The empires' looks and their Mesher
hunks.note: The whole new module: the zone enum (with new GOLD, ACCENT2 and WOOD zones), the per-empire LOOKS table, the cached materials, glass and hologram, and the Mesher class with its part builders, plus crate meshes.

bubbles.at: enum { MAIN, ACCENT, IRON, STEEL, LAMP, SCREEN, ROUNDEL, BANNER, LEATHER, CLOTH, LEAVES, HAZARD, FRIEZE, GOLD, ACCENT2, WOOD }
bubbles.text: A face's zone is written into its vertex colour's red channel (zone / 16); the shader reads it back to decide paint, metal, emblem, frieze or wood.
One material per empire and kind, cached: a whole ship or station is a single draw with a single material.
Station materials light their emblems, friezes and banners themselves so they read on the station's unlit side.

bubbles.at: func slab(pts: PackedVector2Array, xf: Transform3D, t: float, zone: int, edge: int) -> void:
bubbles.text: Triangulates a 2D outline, makes top and bottom faces offset by half the thickness, and walls round the rim in a separate zone.

files.explanation: Deleted. MinoanKit was the Minoan-only version of the ship and station look; everything it did now lives in EmpireKit, which takes the empire as a parameter, so this file was removed rather than kept alongside.

files.explanation: CosmosWalker is you on foot: walking, running, swimming and jumping on a planet's ground or a station's deck. This patch replaces the old jump (which played a combat somersault) with proper jump and fall clips, and adds a jet pack on the automaton's back: holding Space after a jump fires it, climbing while its charge lasts. Its level comes from an automaton upgrade; at the top level it flies without limit, out of the air into space, where gravity weakens with height and the nearest world takes over. Around it come landing dust, a roar, heat haze, fall damage on hard landings, and sitting in the port's chairs and stools.

files.explanation: Cosmos is the 3D scene's root: it builds a star system piece by piece under the loading veil, runs docking, talking, traffic and the ship's calls. In this patch docking no longer cuts to a separate hangar far away: the ship rides its pad's lift 60 m down into a port hall built under the landing platform, and the ships around you stay. It also gains the stations' law (a CosmosLaw child node), dialogue with the port's people and hails from stations in trouble, sitting in seats, the jet-pack pickup (your ship flies to you when you are high up), and several loading-time fixes that spread the last build steps over separate frames.

files.explanation: A new node that holds the stations' law and their guns in the 3D game. It keeps a per-system crime record (debt and remaining wanted time) in the save's extras, fines you for firing on traders and patrols near a station, marks you wanted for destroying one or firing on a station, refuses you a pad while wanted or in debt, aims and fires each station's turrets at you or at invaders and raiders, spawns the ships of invasion fleets besieging the system, makes damaged stations burn, and has stations in trouble hail you.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,348 @@ 
+class_name CosmosLaw
+extends Node
+## The stations' law and their guns, and war at them (the 3D game's).
+##
+## Crime: firing on a trader or a patrol where a station sees it (within
+## NOTICE) - a fine, taken from your credits (what you can't pay a debt: no
+## pad till it's paid). Destroying one of them, or firing on a station, is
+## murder: the system's stations open fire on you (their turrets - CosmosStation.
+## turrets - heavy bolts, GUN_DAMAGE: they will destroy you), its patrols hunt
+## you, for WANTED_TIME or till your ship is lost. Stations of an empire that
+## holds you hostile shoot at you too.
+## War: an empire's invasion fleet besieging your system (Fleets.besiegers) is
+## there in ships - invaders circling the station they besiege, firing on it
+## (Galaxy.damage_station: it burns below Galaxy.DAMAGED - explosions on it); its
+## turrets fire back. Each one destroyed counts for your defence missions
+## (Missions.on_enemy_killed) and against its fleet (Fleets.ship_lost). A
+## station in trouble hails you as you come near (Cosmos.hail_station): its
+## defence and repair jobs, well paid.
+
+const NOTICE := 20000.0          # m: crimes a station sees
+const FINE_ASSAULT := 250        # dr: firing on a trader or a patrol
+const WANTED_TIME := 900.0       # s: the stations' guns on you after murder
+const GUN_RANGE := 4500.0        # m
+const GUN_EVERY := 0.55          # s a turret
+const GUN_DAMAGE := 48.0         # (at you: a few seconds under them is death)
+const GUN_DAMAGE_NPC := 14.0     # (at invaders, raiders)
+const SIEGE_HIT := 0.12          # % of a station's condition an invader's hit takes
+const INVADERS := 5              # ships of a fleet out at once
+const HAIL_NEAR := 30000.0       # m
+
+var cosmos: Node
+var _gun_cd := {}                # turret -> s
+var _hailed := {}                # station id -> true (this visit to the system)
+var _tick := 0.0
+var _burn := 0.0
+var _fined_at := {}              # ship -> time (one fine a few seconds)
+var _rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	_rng.randomize()
+
+
+## This system's record: {"debt": dr, "wanted": s left}.
+func rec(sys := "") -> Dictionary:
+	var all: Dictionary = CosmosGame.extra.get("crime", {})
+	if not CosmosGame.extra.has("crime"):
+		CosmosGame.extra["crime"] = all
+	var id: String = sys if sys != "" else str(cosmos.system_id)
+	if not all.has(id):
+		all[id] = {"debt": 0, "wanted": 0.0}
+	return all[id]
+
+
+func wanted() -> bool:
+	return float(rec().get("wanted", 0.0)) > 0.0
+
+
+func debt() -> int:
+	return int(rec().get("debt", 0))
+
+
+## The station that saw it (the nearest within NOTICE), or null.
+func _witness(p: Vector3) -> CosmosStation:
+	var best: CosmosStation = null
+	for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+		if st.global_position.distance_to(p) < NOTICE and (best == null or st.global_position.distance_to(p) < best.global_position.distance_to(p)):
+			best = st
+	return best
+
+
+## Your bolt hitting `t` (a ship): a crime if it's a trader or a patrol not at war with you.
+func player_hit(t: Node) -> void:
+	if not t is CosmosNpcShip:
+		return
+	var s := t as CosmosNpcShip
+	s.set_meta("by_player", true)
+	if s.kind in ["pirate", "invader"] or Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(s.faction):
+		return
+	var st := _witness(s.global_position)
+	if st == null:
+		return
+	var now := Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
+	if now - float(_fined_at.get(s, -99.0)) < 4.0:
+		return
+	_fined_at[s] = now
+	_fine(st, FINE_ASSAULT, "firing on a %s" % ("patrol" if s.kind == "patrol" else "trader"))
+
+
+func _fine(st: CosmosStation, amount: int, why: String) -> void:
+	var data = CosmosGame.data
+	var paid := mini(amount, int(data.credits))
+	if paid > 0:
+		data.add_credits(-paid)
+	var r := rec()
+	r["debt"] = int(r["debt"]) + amount - paid
+	var who := str(cosmos.label_of(st))
+	cosmos.hud.flash("%s: fined %d dr for %s%s" % [who, amount, why, (" - %d dr owed" % int(r["debt"])) if int(r["debt"]) > 0 else ""], 4.0)
+	GameLog.post("Fined %d dr by %s for %s" % [amount, who, why], "danger")
+	Galaxy.change_reputation(str(st.record.get("empire", "")), -2.0, why)
+
+
+## One of theirs destroyed: by you (it had your bolts in it) - murder.
+func ship_destroyed(s: CosmosNpcShip) -> void:
+	if s.kind == "invader":
+		var fleet := str(s.get_meta("fleet", ""))
+		CosmosGame.missions.on_enemy_killed("warship", s.faction, fleet)
+		if fleet != "":
+			Fleets.ship_lost(fleet)
+		if s.has_meta("by_player"):
+			var b := 300 + _rng.randi_range(0, 200)
+			CosmosGame.data.add_credits(b)
+			var home := s.home as CosmosStation
+			if home and is_instance_valid(home):
+				Galaxy.change_reputation(str(home.record.get("empire", "")), 4.0, "defence")
+			cosmos.hud.flash("%s destroyed - %d dr from the defenders" % [s.label, b], 3.0)
+		return
+	if not s.has_meta("by_player") or s.kind == "pirate" or Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(s.faction):
+		return
+	var st := _witness(s.global_position)
+	if st:
+		_murder(st, "destroying a %s" % ("patrol" if s.kind == "patrol" else "trader"))
+
+
+## Firing on a station: war if you're at war with it (or on a strike mission
+## against it) - it takes the damage; else murder all the same.
+func station_hit(st: CosmosStation, dmg: float) -> void:
+	var sid := str(st.record.get("id", ""))
+	var emp := str(st.record.get("empire", ""))
+	var striking: bool = CosmosGame.missions.active.any(func(m): return m.get("type", "") == "strike" and m.get("station_id", "") == sid)
+	if striking or Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(emp):
+		var pct := dmg * 0.01
+		Galaxy.damage_station(sid, pct)
+		CosmosGame.missions.on_station_hit(sid, pct)
+	if not wanted():
+		_murder(st, "firing on the station")
+
+
+func _murder(st: CosmosStation, why: String) -> void:
+	var r := rec()
+	var first := float(r.get("wanted", 0.0)) <= 0.0
+	r["wanted"] = WANTED_TIME
+	var emp := str(st.record.get("empire", ""))
+	if first:
+		Galaxy.change_reputation(emp, -30.0, why)
+		cosmos.hud.flash("WANTED for %s - the stations of %s will open fire on you" % [why, Galaxy.system(cosmos.system_id).get("name", "this system")], 6.0)
+		GameLog.post("Wanted in %s for %s: its stations' guns are turned on you" % [Galaxy.system(cosmos.system_id).get("name", "?"), why], "danger")
+	for x in cosmos.npc_ships:
+		if is_instance_valid(x) and x.kind == "patrol":
+			x.hostile = true
+
+
+## Your ship lost: the law's done with you here.
+func ship_lost() -> void:
+	var r := rec()
+	r["wanted"] = 0.0
+	r["debt"] = 0
+
+
+## Why `st` won't give you a pad ("" - it will). A debt you can pay is paid.
+func refuses(st: CosmosStation) -> String:
+	if wanted():
+		return "%s refuses you - you're wanted here" % cosmos.label_of(st)
+	if Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(str(st.record.get("empire", ""))):
+		return "%s refuses you - its empire counts you an enemy" % cosmos.label_of(st)
+	var d := debt()
+	if d > 0:
+		if int(CosmosGame.data.credits) >= d:
+			CosmosGame.data.add_credits(-d)
+			rec()["debt"] = 0
+			cosmos.hud.flash("Fine paid: %d dr" % d, 3.0)
+			return ""
+		return "%s refuses you - pay your fine first (%d dr)" % [cosmos.label_of(st), d]
+	return ""
+
+
+## Your bolt from `a` to `b`: into a station's parts? (it hit; true)
+func player_bolt(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, dmg: float) -> bool:
+	for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+		if st.global_position.distance_to(a) > st.reach + 200.0:
+			continue
+		var L := a.distance_to(b)
+		if st.cam_hit(a, (b - a) / maxf(L, 0.001), L) < L:
+			station_hit(st, dmg)
+			return true
+	return false
+
+
+## An invader's bolt (aimed at a point of its station: meta "st", "aim"): there? (true: hit)
+func invader_bolt(bolt: Node3D, a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> bool:
+	var st = bolt.get_meta("st", null)
+	if st == null or not is_instance_valid(st):
+		return true
+	var p: Vector3 = (st as CosmosStation).to_global(bolt.get_meta("aim"))
+	var seg := b - a
+	var t := clampf((p - a).dot(seg) / maxf(seg.length_squared(), 0.0001), 0.0, 1.0)
+	if (a + seg * t).distance_to(p) < 30.0:
+		Galaxy.damage_station(str(st.record.get("id", "")), SIEGE_HIT)
+		if a.distance_to(cosmos.focus().global_position) < 9000.0:
+			CosmosBoom.at(cosmos, p, 10.0)
+		return true
+	return false
+
+
+## A point on `st` to aim at (one of its parts, station space).
+func station_point(st: CosmosStation) -> Vector3:
+	var list: Array = st._solids
+	for k in 6:
+		var s: Array = list[_rng.randi() % list.size()]
+		if not s[0]:
+			return s[1]
+	return Vector3.ZERO
+
+
+# --- Each frame: the guns; a few times a second: sieges, hails, fires --------------
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if cosmos == null or not cosmos.built or get_tree().paused:
+		return
+	var r := rec()
+	if float(r["wanted"]) > 0.0:
+		r["wanted"] = maxf(0.0, float(r["wanted"]) - delta)
+	_guns(delta)
+	_tick -= delta
+	if _tick <= 0.0:
+		_tick = 1.0
+		_sieges()
+		_hails()
+	_burn -= delta
+	if _burn <= 0.0:
+		_burn = _rng.randf_range(0.6, 1.6)
+		_fires()
+
+
+## The turrets: each on the nearest thing it's to fire at, within GUN_RANGE -
+## you (wanted; an enemy's station), invaders, raiders.
+func _guns(delta: float) -> void:
+	var me: Node3D = cosmos.ship
+	var at_me: bool = me.state == "fly" and cosmos.walker == null and not cosmos.docked
+	for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+		if st.turrets.is_empty() or st.global_position.distance_to(cosmos.focus().global_position) > st.reach + GUN_RANGE * 2.0:
+			continue
+		var hate_me := at_me and (wanted() or Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(str(st.record.get("empire", ""))))
+		var foes: Array = []
+		for x in cosmos.npc_ships:
+			if is_instance_valid(x) and not x.dead and (x.kind in ["invader", "pirate"]) and x.global_position.distance_to(st.global_position) < st.reach + GUN_RANGE:
+				foes.append(x)
+		if not hate_me and foes.is_empty():
+			continue
+		for tu: Node3D in st.turrets:
+			var head: Node3D = tu.get_child(1)
+			var muzzle := head.global_position
+			var best: Node3D = null
+			var bd := GUN_RANGE
+			if hate_me and muzzle.distance_to(me.global_position) < bd:
+				best = me
+				bd = muzzle.distance_to(me.global_position) * 0.7   # (you first)
+			for x in foes:
+				var d := muzzle.distance_to(x.global_position)
+				if d < bd:
+					best = x
+					bd = d
+			if best == null:
+				continue
+			var d := muzzle.distance_to(best.global_position)
+			var v: Vector3 = best.get("velocity") if best.get("velocity") != null else Vector3.ZERO
+			var lead: Vector3 = best.global_position + v * (d / CosmosBolt.SPACE_SPEED)
+			var up := st.global_basis.y
+			if (lead - muzzle).normalized().dot(up) < -0.2:
+				continue   # (below its deck: out of its arc)
+			head.look_at(lead, up if absf((lead - muzzle).normalized().dot(up)) < 0.98 else st.global_basis.x)

+				var spread := 0.004
+				var aim := (lead - muzzle).normalized() + Vector3(_rng.randfn(0, spread), _rng.randfn(0, spread), _rng.randfn(0, spread))
+				var bolt := CosmosBolt.fire(cosmos, muzzle - head.global_basis.z * 9.0, aim, "enemy" if best == me else "station",
+					GUN_DAMAGE if best == me else GUN_DAMAGE_NPC, true)

+			_gun_cd[tu] = cd

+## The fleets besieging this system: their ships out round the station they're at.
+func _sieges() -> void:
+	if cosmos.docked or cosmos.walker:
+		return
+	var sys := str(cosmos.system_id)
+	for f in Fleets.in_system(sys):
+		if f["mission"] != "invade" or not (f["route"] as Array).is_empty() or f.get("waiting", false):
+			continue
+		var emp := str(f["empire"])
+		# (its target: the weakest station here of an empire it's at war with)
+		var target: CosmosStation = null
+		for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+			if Galaxy.at_war(emp, Galaxy.station_owner(str(st.record.get("id", "")))):
+				if target == null or Galaxy.station_health(str(st.record.get("id", ""))) < Galaxy.station_health(str(target.record.get("id", ""))):
+					target = st
+		if target == null or target.global_position.distance_to(cosmos.ship.global_position) > 60000.0:
+			continue
+		var out: Array = cosmos.npc_ships.filter(func(x): return is_instance_valid(x) and x.kind == "invader" and str(x.get_meta("fleet", "")) == str(f["id"]))
+		if out.size() >= mini(int(f["size"]), INVADERS) or not CosmosHull.ready("patrol", emp):
+			continue
+		var s := CosmosNpcShip.new()
+		s.setup("invader", cosmos, _rng.randi(), emp)
+		s.set_meta("fleet", str(f["id"]))
+		s.home = target
+		cosmos.world.add_child(s)

+## A station burning or besieged hails you as you come near: its jobs.
+func _hails() -> void:
+	if cosmos.docked or cosmos.walker or cosmos.get_tree().paused or cosmos.ship.state != "fly":
+		return
+	for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+		var sid := str(st.record.get("id", ""))
+		if _hailed.has(sid) or st.global_position.distance_to(cosmos.ship.global_position) > HAIL_NEAR:
+			continue
+		var hurt := Galaxy.station_health(sid) < Galaxy.DAMAGED
+		var siege := Fleets.besieged(sid)
+		if not (hurt or siege) or Galaxy.is_hostile_to_player(str(st.record.get("empire", ""))) or wanted():
+			continue
+		_hailed[sid] = true
+		cosmos.hail_station(st, siege)
+		return
+
+
+## Explosions on stations that are hurt (more the worse they are), near you.
+func _fires() -> void:
+	var f: Vector3 = cosmos.focus().global_position
+	for st: CosmosStation in cosmos.stations:
+		var h := Galaxy.station_health(str(st.record.get("id", "")))
+		if h >= 95.0 or st.global_position.distance_to(f) > st.reach + 12000.0 or st._solids.is_empty():
+			continue

+
+
+## Leaving the system: the next visit's hails anew.
+func new_system() -> void:
+	_hailed.clear()
+	_gun_cd.clear()
+	_fined_at.clear()

files.explanation: CosmosStation builds a space station in the 3D game. It used to be one generic design (a core tower, a spinning ring, docking arms) with a special case for the Minoans; now every empire has its own design taken from its reference sheet (Athens' temples and tholos, Sparta's octagonal fortress, Mycenae's cyclopean citadel, Ionia's armillary, the Cyclades' spiral, the Sea Peoples' broken ring, a plain one for the independents), all in the empire's look from EmpireKit. Its parts are no longer hundreds of MeshInstance3D nodes created and freed during loading: they are plain data (Part), the drawn-only decoration is recorded (Dress) and both are baked into one mesh on a worker thread. The ring holds still, four landing platforms stand out from it, and under each platform hangs a port module (floor, walls, a window band) that CosmosHangar fills in; the station also gets eight gun turrets and its setup can be split over two loading frames.

hunks.note: The header now describes per-empire designs, the old colour table goes, and the port module's dimensions become constants. Two small classes replace the scene nodes: Part (a solid box, cylinder or ball as plain numbers) and Dress (a recorder of decoration calls to replay on the baking worker).

bubbles.text: A Part has the same position/rotation/basis interface as a Node3D so the layout code reads the same, but it is just data - no node is created or freed while loading.
Dress mirrors the Mesher's method names (panel, disc, cyl, boxat, slab) and only appends [name, args] to `ops`; the worker later replays them with callv into the real mesh.
The port's floor sits one lift depth (60 m) below a pad's top, so the lifts stop exactly on it; PORT_INSET keeps the port's inner wall 6 m clear of the ring.

hunks.title: Setup split; one design per empire
hunks.note: setup now picks the empire's design and defers the rest to finish(), which builds the port windows, shutters, turrets, collision solids and starts the bake. The old generic core/ring/arms layout is replaced by small helpers (_arc, _radial, _tiers, _dome, _spike, _frieze, _banner, _roundel, _columns) and a shared _ring_platforms that puts four platforms on the ring's outer face.

bubbles.text: Each empire's builder lays out its own parts and returns [the radius its platforms stand out from, their deck height], so the platforms and ports are common code for every design.

The second loading step: all the ports' window panes go into one SurfaceTool mesh with a two-sided glass material, then turrets, solids and the bake are started; `_finished` guards against running twice.

bubbles.text: Places a box tangent to a circle at angle `a` - the building block of every ring segment, window strip and armour plate.

bubbles.at: var rec := {"centre": centre, "yaw": -a, "pd": pd, "pw": pw, "big": big, "pads": [], "holes": holes}
bubbles.text: Each platform is recorded (centre, facing, size, its pads' holes) so the hangar under it and the turrets can be placed from the same numbers; each pad also remembers its platform.

+		_arc(a, R, -5.0, Vector3(sl * 1.02, 76.0, W * 0.8), "dark")
+		_arc(a, R + (w - W) * 0.25, h * 0.5 - 50.0, Vector3(sl * 0.955, h, w), "hull")
+		var ro := R + (w - W) * 0.25 + w * 0.5
+		if i % 3 == 1:
+			_arc(a, ro + 0.6, 10.0, Vector3(sl * 0.9, 12.0, 2.0), "paint")
+			for q in [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]:
+				_arc(a, ro + 2.0, 10.0, Vector3(7.0, 7.0, 3.0), "trim", q * sl * 0.3)
+		elif i % 3 == 0:

+	_tiers([[-460.0, 40.0, 30.0, 140.0, "dark"], [-360.0, 170.0, 80.0, 140.0, "hull"], [-240.0, 250.0, 60.0, 180.0, "dark"],
